title: Custom Rules dialog renders no rule rows, so Customize and in-game rule editing cannot change any rule

path.to: Custom Game -> pick a map -> Customize (or open_dialog("custom_rules", {"rules": ...}) directly; the port's pause menu has no rules entry)

java: Launch the pinned Java client; open Custom Game, pick any map, press Customize: the dialog shows a search field, a 7-category rail and ~100 editable rows (check/number/team builders, CustomRulesDialog.java:140-206).
Toggle @rules.infiniteresources, close, press Play: the map starts with infinite resources (MapPlayDialog.java:75 applies the edited Rules object).
In a custom game, pause -> the book (customize) button appears when rules are editable and applies the edited Rules on dialog hide (PausedDialog.java:27-37).
godot: Start the Godot client; open Custom Game (PAR-0066 may error in the build window - open_dialog("map_play", {"map": ...}) bypasses it) -> Customize.
Observe: only the 7 category buttons and a category title render - zero rule rows and no search; custom_rules_dialog.gd:49-53 adds exactly one header label and never reads or writes a Rules value.
Pause a custom game: no rules/book entry exists (paused_dialog.gd:44-86 builds only objective/abandon/back/settings/save/load/planet/host/quit).
compare: Java exposes the whole Rules model for editing and hands the edited Rules to playMap/setRules; the Godot dialog cannot read or write a single rule - map_play_dialog.gd:115-118 even documents that the dialog does not produce rules yet.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: client/ui/dialogs/custom_rules_dialog.gd:49 (_rebuild) renders only a header because there is no Rules descriptor/JSON read-write path from the Rules model, and paused_dialog.gd never opens the dialog at all (Java PausedDialog.java:27-34).
plan.approach: 1) Add a rules getter next to MindCampaign.set_rules_json (campaign.rs:782) that serializes the live Rules through mind_core::io::json::rules so the dialog can seed rows and map_play can round-trip edited JSON. 2) Port the CustomRulesDialog row builders (search + category rail + check/number/text/team with enable predicates, CustomRulesDialog.java:122-360) into custom_rules_dialog.gd over a descriptor table of Rules fields; edits accumulate into a local Rules JSON. 3) map_play_dialog._open_rules passes the current rules JSON into the dialog context and stores the edited JSON back into _rules_json when custom_rules closes. 4) Add the paused-dialog book button (visible when allowEditRules && (server || !net.active()), PausedDialog.java:27-37) that opens custom_rules and applies on hide via set_rules_json.
plan.narrow_check: MCP: open_dialog("custom_rules", {"rules": <json>}) -> count editable rows > 0; toggle waves/infinite resources, close, and read the applied rules back through the campaign facade; headless test that an edited field survives the descriptor -> JSON -> Rules round trip.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (ui-dialogs): S2, high confidence. Player impact: the entire custom-rules editing surface is absent - Customize is an empty shell and the pause menu has no rule-edit entry, so custom game and sandbox rule changes are impossible. PAR-0066 only blocks the Custom Game window for the repro; the dialog can be opened directly. Related dialogs but distinct symptoms: PAR-0023 (campaign difficulty), PAR-0024 (launch loadout).

title: Map Play 'Play' neither loads the selected map nor applies the selected gamemode

path.to: Custom Game -> map tile -> Map Play dialog -> Play (or open_dialog("map_play", {"map": "..."}) then Play)

java: Java: Custom Game -> pick a built-in map -> select Sandbox -> Play: the selected map terrain loads and rules become sandbox/infinite resources (MapPlayDialog.java:54-64 builds rules = map.applyRules(mode); :87-93 calls control.playMap(map, rules, playtesting) -> Control.java:400-417).
Modes that are invalid for the map are disabled (MapPlayDialog.java:61), and the playtest flag sets state.playtestingMap (Control.java:413).
godot: Godot: same flow, or open map_play directly; select Sandbox and press Play.

map_play_dialog.gd:88-99 emits play_requested (grep: no listeners anywhere) and calls MindCampaign.start_map(name) because start_map_mode does not exist (line 95 probes has_method; only this file mentions the name).

campaign.rs:662-668 start_map clones session.rules, sets mode_name and calls play_map - the map name is never resolved to terrain and the mode is never applied; the sim host is not reloaded (only load_sector at sim_host.rs:939 loads a grid, and only for campaign sectors).
Observe: the previously loaded world stays (or an empty menu world), and rules keep the prior session values - sandbox shows no infinite resources, PvP/attack flags never set.
compare: Java loads the chosen map file and applies Gamemode rules before play; Godot drops mode/playtest/rules and never touches the world grid, so the Play button is effectively a rules no-op on the old world.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine

plan.approach: 1) Add the load half: MindSimHost.load_map(name, rules_json) resolving the map the same way the Custom Game grid does (Maps/CustomGame registry) and loading its grid through the existing load machinery (load_grid_file sim_host.rs:1786; Maps::load_map_file maps/mod.rs:235). 2) Add MindCampaign.start_map_mode(map, mode, playtest, rules_json): start from the map's own rules (Map::rules maps/map.rs:163), apply Gamemode::apply (gamemode.rs:70), override with rules_json, then call play_map once with those rules and install the runtime the way start_sector does. 3) Make map_play_dialog._play require start_map_mode and fail loudly instead of the silent start_map fallback (line 97-99); keep _rules_json synced from Customize. 4) Carry the playtest flag (Control.java:413 state.playtestingMap + resumeAfterPlaytest) or route the editor's playtest through MindEditor.playtest (editor/mod.rs:1106). 5) Disable invalid modes with Gamemode::valid(map) (gamemode.rs:108), matching MapPlayDialog.java:61.

PAR-0065 covers only the map grid, PAR-0066 the dialog build panic - both distinct.

title: Load Game 'Import Save' does nothing: no .msav is imported after picking a file

path.to: Pause (non-campaign) or menu -> Load Game -> @save.import -> pick a .msav in the fallback file chooser

java: Java: pause -> Load Game -> Import Save -> chooser filtered to msav -> picking a valid .msav imports it into the slot grid (LoadDialog.java:199-223); invalid saves show @save.import.invalid and campaign saves @save.nocampaign.
godot: Godot: Load Game -> @save.import -> file_chooser opens with no extension filter (load_dialog.gd:259-264 passes only {"open": true}).

Click a file: file_chooser_dialog.gd:95-98 emits file_chosen and hides, but no node is connected (grep client/) - only editor_maps_dialog.gd:144-147 listens - so the slot grid never refreshes and no slot is created. No error is shown either.

Saves.import_save exists in mind-core (saves.rs:406-423) but has no GDExt binding (grep import_save under client/rust/mind-gdext -> none); the drag-drop classifier platform/desktop.rs:59-78 only logs and returns true.
compare: Java imports the picked file through control.saves.importSave and rebuilds the grid; Godot emits the path into the void and the file is silently discarded (button and chooser both look functional).

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: client/ui/dialogs/load_dialog.gd:259 (_open_import) never listens to file_chooser.file_chosen, and there is no GDExt import_save binding; Saves::import_save (mind-core saves.rs:406) is dead code.
plan.approach: 1) Expose MindCampaign.import_save(path) calling Saves::import_save (saves.rs:406) through the same settings/paths/filesystem handles list_save_slots uses; return an error kind so the dialog can show @save.import.invalid / @save.nocampaign. 2) In load_dialog._open_import, connect the file_chooser file_chosen (and chooser_cancelled) before opening, pass extensions ["msav"], call import_save on selection, then refresh the grid or show the error toast. 3) Route the existing dropped-file path (platform/desktop.rs:59 handle_file_import) into import_save instead of the log-only branch.
plan.narrow_check: Headless: copy a fixture .msav to a temp dir -> import_save -> list_save_slots grows by one and loading it round-trips the same checksum; importing a junk file returns the invalid error. MCP: pick a .msav in the chooser -> a row appears in the Load Game grid.

Player impact: saves cannot be brought in from outside the client; upstream's Import Save is the documented migration path. The fallback chooser itself is otherwise wired (navigation/extension filter), only the import end is missing. Distinct from PAR-0024/PAR-0037 (launch/save-resume flows).

title: Choosing a language shows the restart prompt but is never persisted - the UI stays English after restart

path.to: Menu -> Settings -> Language (or the settings category action) -> click a language -> restart the client

java: Java: Settings -> Language -> click Deutsch: settings 'locale' is written, player.locale updates, the restart prompt shows; after restart the UI is German (LanguageDialog.java:78-83).
godot: Godot: Settings -> Language -> click Deutsch: language_dialog.gd:72-77 emits locale_selected and shows @language.restart.

locale_selected has no listener (grep client/** -> only the signal declaration and the emit), and the locale key the bundle reads (LOCALE_SETTING = "mindustry/locale", assets/loader.rs:18-29) is never written anywhere (grep mindustry/locale -> read-only).
After restart the bundle is still English and project setting mindustry/locale is unset; re-opening the dialog shows English selected.
compare: Java persists locale in Core.settings and the next boot resolves it; Godot's dialog is a UI shell whose only effect is the info toast.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine
plan.seam: client/ui/dialogs/language_dialog.gd:72 (_select) emits an unconnected signal; assets/loader.rs:18 LOCALE_SETTING is read-only, so the selection never reaches the bundle resolution.
plan.approach: 1) Add a MindUi.set_locale(locale) (or connect locale_selected in ui_root's dialog-intent wiring) that writes ProjectSettings "mindustry/locale" and saves it, plus the Core.settings-parity 'locale' value. 2) language_dialog._select calls it before showing @language.restart and tracks the chosen locale as current so the row renders checked. 3) No runtime bundle swap is needed - the atlas already loads the bundle from resolve_locale() at boot (assets/atlas.rs:163), matching upstream's restart requirement.
plan.narrow_check: MCP: select de -> ProjectSettings.get_setting("mindustry/locale") == "de"; relaunch -> MindAssets.bundle_get("@settings") returns the German string and re-opening the dialog shows de checked.

note: Code-scan 2026-10-10 (ui-dialogs): S3, high confidence. Player impact: locale selection is inert - the player picks a language, is told to restart, and gets English again; non-English players cannot use the translated bundles already shipped in assets/locales. The locale list itself renders from MindAssets.locales().

title: Join Game forgets added servers and the Remote server list is always empty

path.to: Menu -> Join Game -> @server.add -> type an address -> OK -> restart the client -> Join Game again

java: Java: Join Game -> @server.add -> enter an ip -> OK: the server is persisted to settings (JoinDialog.java:106 saveServers, :773-775) and appears under @servers.remote with ping/map details (section :328, refreshRemote :237-256).
Restart the client: loadServers (:64-70, :689-691) restores the list and the saved server still renders.
godot: Godot: Join Game -> @server.add -> address -> OK: _submit_add (join_dialog.gd:301-307) only emits connect_requested; there is no settings read/write anywhere in the dialog.

The @servers.remote group body is a fixed 4px spacer (join_dialog.gd:110-112), and the local list consumes _context['servers'] (:184) which no live caller ever supplies (menu_fragment.gd:36/54 opens join with an empty context).
After restart the address is gone and the Remote group is still blank; there is no edit/delete/reorder for saved servers.
compare: Java persists and lists saved servers (settings-backed) independent of the transport; Godot's add flow is fire-and-forget and its Remote section has no data source at all.

plan.state: seeded by code-scan 2026-10-10; not yet verified in-engine

plan.approach: 1) Add a JSON accessor pair to the settings store (e.g. MindUi.servers_json()/set_servers_json() over SettingsStore, mirroring Core.settings.getJson("servers")); ui_host.rs:614 settings_set is the existing seam. 2) Load the list on ready/shown and render each entry in the Remote body with connect (connect_requested) and delete actions; persist on add and delete. 3) Keep the local group honest: LAN discovery (net.discoverServers) has no SpacetimeDB equivalent, so leave @hosts.none instead of faking rows. 4) Add the rename/edit path and row reordering (JoinDialog.java:106-117, :217-235) after persistence exists.

title: Server Bans/Admins management is dead: player-list entries open nothing and the dialogs have no roster or unban/unadmin action

path.to: In a live match: toggle the player list (Tab upstream) -> @server.bans / @server.admins

java: Java: in an active match press Tab -> the player list opens; @server.bans renders a row per ban with an unban (cancel) button + confirm (BansDialog.java:30-55, :43-44); @server.admins un-admins the same way (AdminsDialog.java:30-58, :43-44); both are disabled for clients (PlayerListFragment.java:65-66).
godot: The player list cannot be opened: the PLAYER_LIST binding (binding.rs:769, Tab) has no consumer - desktop.rs:555-563 maps only minimap/console and ui_root.gd handles only ESC/M/F8 - so Tab does nothing.

If the fragment is shown by hand, its menu buttons call _open("@server.bans") -> trim_prefix("@") -> ui.open_dialog("server.bans") (player_list_fragment.gd:86-100); the registry names are 'bans'/'admins' (dialogs_manifest.json:27-28), so ui_host.rs:181-186 logs "unknown dialog 'server.bans'" and returns false. No dialog opens.
Even opened directly, admins_dialog.gd:26-36 / bans_dialog.gd:25-35 render only label rows from a _context that no caller supplies (empty state forever) and have no unban/unadmin button.
compare: Java: the player list is reachable in any match and both dialogs read NetServer.admins and perform unban/unadmin with confirm. Godot: unreachable list, unregistered dialog names, no roster source, no actions.
